title: Let an identity column make an id
summary: An IDENTITY column generates numeric values for new rows.
introduction: An IDENTITY column generates numeric values for new rows. Your task: Insert a second book and read the returned id.
learningObjectives: Insert a second book and read the returned id.
Explain the example for let an identity column make an id

blocks.text: An IDENTITY column generates numeric values for new rows. OUTPUT can show the id that was actually inserted.
Use SQL Server 2019+ in a separate practice database with a SQL editor. T-SQL is different from the SQLite engine on this site, so these examples are for that separate tool.

items: A primary key identifies a row and prevents duplicate key values. Related records can refer to that key.

blocks.text: The inserted sample row is returned with its generated id and title.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not assume identity values are gap-free. Failed or removed rows can leave gaps.
